content.overview: Save as otherwise provided in sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 378D, every Member shall have one vote and in the case of equality of votes, the Chairman or the person presiding shall have a casting vote except in the case of election of the Chairman.
content.glance: One Member, one vote (subject to s. 378D); Chairman has a casting vote on equality, except when electing the Chairman.
content.study: Section 378Z states the default voting rule for Members of a Producer Company: one vote per Member, subject to the special rules in section 378D(1) and (3). On equality of votes the Chairman or person presiding has a casting vote, except when the election of the Chairman itself is being decided.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: Every Member has one vote (subject to s. 378D); on equality the Chairman or person presiding has a casting vote, except in the election of the Chairman.

examples.title: Illustration — s. 378Z
examples.body: At a general meeting with an equal split of votes, the Chairman casts a deciding vote under s. 378Z, unless the question is the election of the Chairman.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 378Z?
hypotheticals.analysis: It fixes one-Member-one-vote as the default, with a casting vote for the Chairman except on election of the Chairman.

misconceptions.trap: Treating this section as a dispute-resolution provision.
misconceptions.correction: s. 378Z is Voting rights; dispute resolution is a different provision.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 378Z be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Apply one-Member-one-vote (subject to s. 378D). II. Note the casting-vote rule and its exception. III. Conclude.

examTips: Name s. 378Z: Voting rights (one Member, one vote).
revisionPoints: Voting rights — one Member one vote; Chairman casting vote except on election of Chairman
